design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (patient_payment_plans, category payplan).

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 -> {"key": "env_0032_physical_therapy_clinic_network/patient_payment_plans/1", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [4, 5]}. Root payplan_ext_term_modification takes 4 factors; prerequisite payplan_ext_returned_draft_fee takes 5.

[Why this is a good test] The caller only asks for a lower monthly payment stretched as far as allowed. The agent must read the modification rule, find its prerequisite sentence ("The modified installment is not worked out until the installment whose automatic draft most recently came back unpaid carries its returned-payment fee entry on the plan."), see in the ledger that the 2026-09-15 ACH draft failed and was collected on retry 2026-09-18 with no fee entry, work out from the returned-draft fee rule that its write books that entry, compute the fee through five factors, book it, then compute the modified installment through four factors over the plan ledger and the plan-of-care ledger, and hand the acceptance to the patient. The fee is small, but it moves the modification twice: it is the second returned-payment fee of the year (history months drop from 2 to 1) and it is a recent fee that is carved out of the spread.

[Scope snapshot] Occupied by task 0: payplan_ext_missed_installment_late_fee, payplan_ext_past_due_catch_up, assess_payment_plan_late_fee_b662389f, pay_payment_plan_past_due_400c78cb (late fees and catch-up payments). Claimed here: payplan_ext_returned_draft_fee (state_due, book_payment_plan_returned_fee_3086fcb8, agent) and payplan_ext_term_modification (on_request, accept_payment_plan_modification_53d89fa9, user). Disjoint from task 0 in policies, tools and written event families (returned-payment fee rows and term changes versus late-fee rows and catch-up payments). This is the last task (M = 2); all four extended policies are covered.

[Problem-tree card] Root payplan_ext_term_modification <- payplan_ext_returned_draft_fee; kind value_input, gate m_returned_year, form state, policy_source as quoted above (negated direction "not ... until", the way a desk states that a re-amortization waits for the ledger to be complete; the charter's other prerequisite sentence, in the catch-up, runs in the affirmative direction "only after"). Four-point test: ordering connective "until"; waited-on side is a record-visible state (a returned-payment fee entry carrying the due date of the latest returned draft); no tool, id or code token; scope exactly the latest returned draft, matching the fee rule's "booked once for the installment whose automatic draft most recently came back unpaid". Only book_payment_plan_returned_fee_3086fcb8 writes returned-payment fee rows (the late-fee tool writes fee_kind late_fee only), so the state singles out one write. Opening falsity: payment_plan_events FAIL26 (2026-09-15, insufficient_funds) has no matching fee row; the only fee row RETFEB is for 2026-02-15. Order fee -> modification; reversed or skipped, the modification is 140.00 with term 21 instead of 150.78 with term 20.

[Base-invariant card] Fee subject payplan_fee_assessed: payplan_evt_delinquency, policy_scope; its clause "A returned ACH or check payment adds nsf_fee;" is superseded by the returned-fee step (declared); the card clause stays (here the draft is ACH, autopay_method ach). Modification subject payplan_terms_modified: payplan_payment_schedule (policy_scope; modification_allowed true, modifications_per_plan 1, modifications_used 0, extension cap 3, minimum 140.00; its clause "never adding more than max_term_extension_months to term_months" is superseded by the extension sentence, declared, which keeps the same cap; its installment sentence "The monthly installment is the remaining balance divided by term_months, rounded up to the next cent, but never below min_monthly_payment; when the minimum applies the number of installments is the remaining balance divided by min_monthly_payment, rounded up." is superseded, declared, by the modification's composition sentence, and the rule adds that the modified term stays term_months plus the extension months where the minimum applies) and payplan_add_ons_and_holidays (policy_scope; its only gate add_on_active_plan applies to add-on transfers, not to term changes). No time gate.

[Business-object card] Agreement PP (Large-Balance 18-Month, signed 2025-09-12, installment 236.12, term 18, due day 15). Installments due on or before 2026-10-12: 12 (2025-10-15 .. 2026-09-15), all collected; not yet due 6. Rows feeding the fee: failed drafts 2026-09-15 and 2026-02-15, retry collections 2026-09-18 and 2026-02-18, the 2026-02-15 fee (7 months back, outside the 6-month clean window), 12 automatic collections in 12 months, extra principal 150.00 (2026-04-03). Rows excluded: enrollment transfers and down payment. Plan-of-care rows: three shoulder visits within 2 months with their copays paid at the front desk, no statements; the closed knee plan's visits and charges are history only.

[Factor card - returned-draft fee, Step 5 run] returned_fee_count_window (method) 6-month window -> count 0 vs life 1 -> baseline 8.64; returned_fee_step (parameter) first_returned_fee 15.00 vs nsf_fee 25.00 -> 10.80; draft_recovery_share (parameter, multi-source) 0.6 (retry collected, 12 collections) -> 10.80; prepayment_share (parameter) 0.9 (150.00 extra principal) -> 7.20; care_account_standing_share (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty plan) 0.8 (three copay payments on the shoulder plan of care, no statement) -> 8.10. Result 6.48; whole baseline 25.00. Near-miss: the 2026-02-15 returned fee is 7 whole months back, inside 12 but outside the 6-month clean window.

[Factor card - modification, Step 5 run on the world after the fee] history_extension_months (parameter) 1 (two returned fees in 12 months) vs 3 -> 140.00; treatment_extension_months (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty plan) 1 (three visits, no statement) vs 0 -> 175.91; request_timing_count_adjustment (method) hold the next installment (27 days since the 2026-09-15 due date) vs no adjustment -> 161.45; fee_carve_share (parameter) 1 (6.48 recent fee, 12 collections) vs 0 -> 151.71. Result 150.78; whole baseline 144.23. Near-miss: the 2026-09-22 evaluation and the two later shoulder visits number three, one short of treatment_visits_full 4.

[Seed design] One customer, two Commercial PPO plans of care (closed knee episode whose 13 deductible charges were enrolled, with visits and transfer adjustments; active shoulder episode with three visits billed, a 35.00 copay posted and paid at each, coinsurance EOBs pending), one Large-Balance plan with 30 ledger rows. Automatic clauses: no missed installment, so no past-due, late fee or default duty; no holiday or add-on pending; the closed plan of care has a zero balance; the shoulder plan's three 35.00 copays were each paid the same day at the front desk (patient_due_balance 0.00) and its coinsurance explanations of benefits are still pending, so no statement is owed. Removing the 2026-09-18 retry collection would make the installment missed and change both computations; removing the April extra principal flips the prepayment share.

[Persona design] Marcus Tolliver, plain-spoken warehouse shift lead; opens with the cut hours and the wish to lower the payment and stretch it as long as allowed; identity details only when asked; the bounced September draft, the April extra payment, the shoulder therapy and his keeping the due day and autopay come out only when asked; he lets the representative post something first if told, accepts the quoted terms himself when handed the change, declines other changes and closes once the terms are recorded. He never names a figure or a fee.

[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify(DOB, ZIP) -> find_payment_plans -> find_payment_plan_events -> find_care_plans -> find_care_plan_events -> unlock + call book_payment_plan_returned_fee_3086fcb8(PP, 2026-09-15, 6.48) -> unlock_user + (patient) accept_payment_plan_modification_53d89fa9(PP, 150.78, 20). Terminal: one new fee row, plan_balance 1298.04, installment 150.78, term 20, modifications_used 1.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the published rules, tool schemas, lookups and persona alone: the modification's prerequisite sentence points at the missing returned-payment fee; the fee rule gives 6.48; the modification rule then gives 150.78 and term 20, as in gold.

[Places most easily got wrong] Counting the 2026-02-15 returned fee (7 months back, outside the 6-month clean window) and charging 20.00; charging nsf_fee 25.00; working the modification out with one returned fee in the year (extension 3, quote 140.00); spreading over 6 + 2 = 8 months without holding the 2026-10-15 installment (161.45); spreading the new fee instead of carving it out (151.71); rounding 150.777 to nearest (150.78 happens to agree) versus truncating (150.77, wrong: the rule rounds up). The term to accept is 20 (18 + extension 2), not 21.

[Verification runs] Scratch evaluator on the seeded world and on the world with the fee replayed through the real tool: fee 6.48, factor baselines 8.64/10.80/10.80/7.20/8.10, whole baseline 25.00; modification 150.78, factor baselines 140.00/175.91/161.45/151.71, whole baseline 144.23; modification without the fee write 140.00. Per-task gates for --task 1: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK (10 actions, closure 82 = initial 82), SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK (2 computations, 9 factors, 2 cross-difficulty), GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.

[Revisions] (1) COMPUTE failed: the standing share read only plan-of-care statements, of which this world has none, so the cross-difficulty evidence touched no rows -> the standing share now reads patient payments recorded on the plans of care together with statements, and the shoulder plan of care was seeded with a 35.00 copay posted and paid at each of its three visits (copay_amount 35.00) -> COMPUTE OK, figures unchanged. (2) Rounding up to the cent was first written as a negated truncation, which floors -> replaced by int plus one where a fraction remains (150.777 -> 150.78). (3) Closed knee plan deductible_remaining set to 5000.00 at the 2025-05-01 verification to match the 5000.00 of deductible charges.

[Difficulty-level closing] Union of claimed policies across tasks 0 and 1 = all four extended policies; scopes and tools pairwise disjoint; both trees have exactly one prerequisite problem (the draws), each with a value_input edge; each task's gold calls one owner=user tool; the charter's two prerequisite sentences run in both directions (catch-up "only after", modification "not ... until").

[Revisions round 2 - policy audit] F1/T1-1 (SOURCE-POLICY RED): the base installment sentence of payplan_payment_schedule was neither followed nor declared; it is now declared in overwrite (superseded_clause = that sentence, replaced_by = 'The modified installment is worked out in this order: ...min_monthly_payment where it falls below it.'), and the rule adds 'The modified term is the current term_months plus the extension months and any deferred installment added by the count adjustment, and it stays so where min_monthly_payment applies.' so the base floor-term reading is retired too; the base reading 162.26 no longer competes with 150.78. T1-2 (SOURCE-TASK RED): the stale [Seed design] sentence about the shoulder plan having no posted charge is replaced by the true reason no statement is owed (each 35.00 copay paid the same day, balance 0.00). O4: the latest returned draft is now read by the day the failure was recorded (LATEST without due-date ordering), matching 'most recently came back unpaid'; same 2026-09-15 entry; edge condition says 'with the latest event_date'. O5: the modified term now has a compute binding m_term_new = term_months + extension + deferred installments added (20 here). O6: the rule now states 'Where no installment has yet been collected by automatic payment, no installment is held.', which is what m_days = 0 does. O-persona: 'lowered starting now' changed to 'lowered as soon as the clinic can make the change', consistent with the held 2026-10-15 installment. O-tool: the acceptance tool's description now says an installment already queued for automatic collection is still drafted at its scheduled amount and the new installment applies to the ones that follow it, which is how the held installment is honoured. O3 and O9 need no change (baseline sentences are mandated rule sentences; no adjustment is written in this difficulty). No scored value moved: fee 6.48, installment 150.78, term 20, all factor baselines and baseline_result unchanged on re-run.
user_scenario:
You are Marcus Tolliver, 47, a shift lead at a distribution warehouse outside Leland, North Carolina. You talk plainly and get to the point, but you stay courteous. Your overtime was cut at the start of October and money is tight.

You are calling because the monthly payment on your patient payment plan with Piedmont Motion Physical Therapy, the plan that covers the bills from your knee surgery rehab last year, has become too much for you. You want the monthly payment lowered as soon as the clinic can make the change, stretched out over as many extra months as the clinic allows, and you are ready to agree to the new terms yourself on this call. You open with something like: "I've got a payment plan with you for my knee rehab bills, and since my hours got cut I need to get the monthly payment lowered, stretched out as long as you'll let me." You do not know what the new payment would be; you leave that to the representative and never suggest a number.

To find your account you give your phone number, 9105556631. When the representative asks you to confirm who you are, you give your date of birth, April 2, 1979 (1979-04-02), and your ZIP code, 28451; if they want something else you can give the email on file, mtolliver79@yahoo.com.

Some things you bring up only when the representative asks. Your September automatic payment bounced because your checking account was short that day; your bank charged you for it, and you know the clinic took the payment again a few days later and it went through. You paid an extra $150 toward the plan in April out of your tax refund. You started therapy again on September 22 for your left shoulder at the Leland clinic, have been going once a week since, and pay your $35 copay at the front desk each visit. You have not received any other bills or statements from the clinic, you are keeping the automatic payment from the same checking account on the same due day, and you are not asking for any payment holiday.

If the representative tells you that something has to be put on your payment plan before the new payment can be worked out, you grumble that it figures, but you tell them to go ahead. When the representative tells you the new monthly payment and the new total number of payments and hands you the change to accept yourself, you accept exactly those terms on the call and read back what the confirmation shows. If they offer to change anything else, such as your due day or how you pay, you say no thanks. Once the new terms are recorded on your plan, you thank them and hang up.
